newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatar to open first stock market on May 27.
newsitem.headline: Qatar to open first stock market on May 27.

text.p: Qatar's first official stock exchange will start operations on May 27, the bourse's chairman Youssef Hussein Kamal said on Tuesday.
Initially, only Qatari nationals would be allowed to trade in shares listed on the Doha Securities Market (DSM), he said in a press statement.
Officials have earlier said Gulf Arabs would be allowed to participate in the bourse at a later stage, followed by other foreigners.
Kamal, also undersecretary at Qatar's Ministry of Finance, Trade and Economy, said the market would operate from Sunday to Thursday.
"Working hours will be from 9 a.m. to 10.30 a.m.," he said.
The tiny Gulf Arab state last month moved a step closer towards opening the bourse by appointing Qatar National Bank, Doha Bank Ltd and the Commercial Bank of Qatar as brokers.
He said a DSM committee was processing applications from 20 other firms to select three more brokers.
At present investors trade in the shares of 18 companies by telephone through some banks or private brokers.
DSM officials expect market capitalisation to rise considerably from the present $1.9 billion after the opening.
The bourse, to operate on a semi-electronic basis, would become fully electronic by the second half of next year.
Officials said the bourse would also be dealing in bonds and treasury bills that the government might issue in the future to raise funds from the local market.

The DSM will be the fifth formal bourse in the six-nation Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC). Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, Bahrain and Oman all have stock exchanges and the United Arab Emirates has an unofficial bourse.
